newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise on London Club debt news.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise on London Club debt news.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose on Friday on news that nearly all of the Russian debt from the Soviet Union to the London Club had been committed by creditors, dealers said.

Germany's Deutsche Bank AG, chair of the London Club of creditors, said that virtally all of the Russian debt from the Soviet Union era eligible to participate in a rescheduling has been committed by creditors.
Deutsche said reconciliation of the committed debt was underway.
Dealers said trading had been quiet earlier, with the market marking time after Wednesday and Thursday's rise on the news President Boris Yeltsin is likely to be operated on in 6-8 weeks.

"Volumes traded are low today as people were having a break after the rise... But generally a Western investment interest is felt as almost all bids seen on the market are from abroad," an ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said.
Prices rose 0.5 points after Deutsche Bank's recheduling news, dealers said.

They added trading in Russia started from levels higher than late Thursday after International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus said the health problems of Yeltsin had not affected distribution of IMF loans to Russia.

"Prices rose late yesterday and it seems like London and New York were buying after Camdessus's comments. They rose another 0.5 point after Deutsche Bank's announcement but have eased a little afterwards," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.
He said the third, fourth and fifth tranches had run into resistance at 78.00, 52.85 and 34.65 bid respectively. The sixth and seventh tranches, issued this May, are less liquid.
